sources.title: Trump offers $1 million for tipoffs leading to vote fraud conviction as midterms approach

en.title: Trump Announces $1 Million Reward for Voter‑Fraud Tips
en.dek: President Trump offers $1 million for tips that lead to voter‑fraud convictions ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.
facts: President Trump announced a $1 million reward for information that leads to a conviction for voter fraud.
The announcement was posted on Truth Social on October 26, 2026.
Trump did not provide details on how the reward would be funded or administered.
Trump has repeatedly made false claims that he won the 2020 presidential election.
Studies find voter fraud extremely rare; an Associated Press investigation in 2020 identified fewer than 475 potential cases.
White House press officer replied to inquiries with "Refer to the TRUTH".
The Justice Department indicted 10 non‑U.S. citizens for alleged voting in the 2024 North Carolina election.
body: On October 26, 2026, President Donald Trump announced a $1 million reward for anyone who could provide information that leads to a conviction for voter fraud in past or upcoming elections.

Trump posted the offer on his Truth Social account, stating that "Anybody reporting Voter Fraud in the past Elections, or the upcoming 2026 Midterm Election, will be paid $1,000,000 upon the arrest and conviction of those that created the Fraud!".
The White House did not disclose how the reward would be funded or how it would be administered. A White House press officer responded to a request for more details with "Refer to the TRUTH."

Voter fraud cases are extremely rare; an Associated Press investigation in 2020 found fewer than 475 potential cases across six battleground states, a figure that would not have changed the outcome of that election.
The Justice Department has indicted 10 non‑U.S. citizens for alleged voting in the 2024 North Carolina election, a case that Trump has highlighted in his recent statements.
The announcement comes as Trump continues to challenge the legitimacy of recent elections and seeks to influence voter sentiment ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.
en.context: Trump has repeatedly claimed election fraud and that he won the 2020 election, despite evidence to the contrary. He is using the reward announcement as a tactic to influence voter perception before the 2026 midterms.
